quote: One of the value-added qualities of Jacobs is the maintenance program. As an example, the Traverse City Wastewater Treatment Plant filter membrane operation has exceeded the life expectancy because of the maintenance program the Jacobs put in place. This is just one aspect of the entire project which has been under the guidance of Jacobs for 29 plus years.
speaker: Richard Lewis, Traverse City Council Commissioner

quote: A key to the delivery success, and to accomplishing the three major goals, was the partnering sessions at the beginning of the project, and the true partnership between the County’s project manager and the Jacobs management team that continued throughout the design-build phase of the project. This was the first Design-Build-Operate project for Spokane County, and the largest public works project ever completed by the County, and we are very satisfied with the results.
speaker: Bruce Rawls, PE, Spokane County Utilities Director

quote: Our MBR process produces great quality water for Title 22 reuse. Good screening at the head of the plant is important to keep material from fouling the membranes. Properly maintaining the blowers and the aeration system is the other big piece of it, because good air scour is critical. Nobody wants to replace membranes early–they are expensive! In general, there are more instruments that need to be calibrated and maintained, and operators will need to learn some new things. But once you learn the process, the system is easy to run.
speaker: Tony Duffy, Jacobs Plant Manager at the Clovis ST/WRF
